doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

title: The Beatles in Liverpool and Basie's Beatle album
summary: Hughes recalls meeting the future Beatles in a Liverpool club in 1964 and later Basie's Beatle Bag.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: In the mid-60’s, and this was just prior to The Beatles striking it big, and the big beat turning things around.

Let me tell you a story about The Beatles. We were in Liverpool in early 1964. And we went to this little cave-like club, you know, and I guess that was them playing. They came back later and said it was them anyhow. We were sitting there and listening to this little group play, you know? And they sounded all right, but we didn’t, you know, pay that much attention. We were really there looking for something else anyhow. And Basie was there. And I remember one of those guys coming up after the set and talking to Basie, asking how he thought they sounded. He say, “yeah,” you know Basie was always very nice, “you guys sound all right” you know? And I think about maybe six months
later, these guys were coming to New York taking New York by storm, you know? And I didn’t realize then it was the same group.
That’s right they were playing The Cavern or something.
But I’ll tell you what they did, they were so impressed with Basie that later on down the line they got Basie to do two Beatle albums. I don’t know whether you ever heard.

“Basie’s Beatle Bag,” and something else, I can’t remember because we never really played the tunes after we did the album. But I remember one of the, I can’t remember whether it was Lennon or somebody else came to the record date while we were doing it. But they had never forgotten that Basie had come in and said that they sounded good.
